title: Ethiopian Spiced Tea
community: All of Ethiopia — the spiced tea of the highlands
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Spiced Tea — black tea brewed with cardamom, cinnamon, ginger, and cloves, served with sugar and optionally with milk. Ethiopia's spiced tea tradition — less elaborate than the coffee ceremony but equally important in Muslim-majority areas where tea is preferred.
longDesc: Ethiopian spiced tea (shai) is the daily drink of the country's Muslim communities and increasingly popular across the entire country. Made with black tea and the Ethiopian spice tradition, it produces a warming, aromatic brew that rivals chai in complexity.
ingredients: 4 tsp loose black tea (or 4 tea bags)
// Optional: 1 cup milk for masala chai style
steps: Add cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, and ginger.
Add tea. Steep off the heat 3—4 minutes.
Add milk if using. Sweeten to taste.
chefTips: Bruise the cardamom pods before adding — releases more flavour.
Do not over-steep the tea — bitter.
Ethiopian shai is often lighter in colour than Indian chai — adjust steeping time.
cookingScience: See TZA221 for spiced tea science.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian-grown cinnamon, ginger, and cardamom are available.
culturalNote: Ethiopian spiced tea is the Muslim community's daily ritual equivalent to the coffee ceremony — the warm, spiced cup that marks the beginning of the day, the breaking of Ramadan fast, and every social gathering. In Harar and Dire Dawa, spiced tea houses are as central to social life as coffee shops in the Christian highlands.
